body: I've had a report of a similar problem of the d3d12 backend instantly crashing on proton for an AMD user on an exported project which seems very similar to this bug report, in my case they were using an RX 6600 GPU. Vulkan also worked fine for that user. 4.7.2 on a desktop platform for the tester as far as I know, I could get more details if its helpful
If they are up for doing the reproduction steps, it could help to make sure it's reproducible on any AMD GPU and not just the Steam Deck.

I can confirm that this is happening on AMD GPUs outside of the steam deck. 

For any folks that want to collect Proton logs to repro this, update the Godot Engine launch args to be `PROTON_LOG=1 %command%`. The log file (which should be named `steam-404790.log`) will be produced in your home directory. 

```
❯ fastfetch
OS: CachyOS x86_64
Kernel: Linux 7.2.0-1-cachyos
CPU: AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D (16) @ 5.27 GHz
GPU 1: AMD Radeon RX 6800 XT [Discrete]
GPU 2: AMD Radeon Graphics [Integrated]
Memory: 20.76 GiB / 61.91 GiB (34%)
```

[steam-404790.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31745801/steam-404790.log)

I have an AMD GPU and was able to reproduce a crash, but I'm not 100% sure if it is related. The crash happens from GE Proton 11.5 and below, but I did testing on 7.55 since newer versions are very debugger unfriendly. I ran the `bullet_showers` project from the demo repos once normally, once with `VK_LAYER_LUNARG_api_dump`, and once with a debugger attached.

Unfortunately, my logs are significantly shorter, and the debugger shows the crash at  to `D3D12GetInterface` (???). The last command I observe is `vkCreateComputePipelines`, but it runs successfully. I hope the data is useful to someone.

System information:
```
Godot v4.7.2.stable unknown - Void https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Mon Aug 10 23:38:14 UTC 2026 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - integrated AMD Radeon 780M Graphics - AMD Ryzen 7 7840U w/ Radeon 780M Graphics (16 threads) - 30.66 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)
```

Commands:

```
# Tested on Godot bullet_showers demo 
SteamGameId=100 PROTON_LOG=1 STEAM_COMPAT_CLIENT_INSTALL_PATH="$HOME/.local/share/Steam" STEAM_COMPAT_DATA_PATH="$(pwd)/.proton" "~/.local/share/Steam/compatibilitytools.d/GE-Proton11-5/proton" run bulletshower.exe --rendering-driver d3d12
# ---
STEAM_COMPAT_CLIENT_INSTALL_PATH="$HOME/.local/share/Steam" STEAM_COMPAT_DATA_PATH="$(pwd)/.proton" "~/.local/share/Steam/compatibilitytools.d/GE-Proton7-55/proton" run winedbg.exe bulletshower.exe --rendering-driver d3d12
# ---
# Requires VulkanTools
export VK_LAYER_PATH=~/pkgs/VulkanTools/build/layersvt:$VK_LAYER_PATH
export VK_INSTANCE_LAYERS=VK_LAYER_LUNARG_api_dump
STEAM_COMPAT_CLIENT_INSTALL_PATH="$HOME/.local/share/Steam" STEAM_COMPAT_DATA_PATH="$(pwd)/.proton" "~/.local/share/Steam/compatibilitytools.d/GE-Proton7-55/proton" run winedbg.exe bulletshower.exe --rendering-driver d3d12
```

[steam-100.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32879965/steam-100.log)
[gdblog.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32879967/gdblog.log)

I also have some AMD GPU's.  I used to be able to reproduce a crash with proton and d3d12.  It was crashing due to some invalid spir-v generated by vkd3d12.  That seems to have been fixed since I last tried.  I'm using current proton-experimental and I can get into the editor now though menus do not work.  Using single-window mode makes them work though.  I can run my texture-streaming demo project now.

Godot v4.8.dev (3ac570a4d) - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Single-window, 2 monitors (2560x1440 @ 120.00 Hz, 2560x1440 @ 120.00 Hz) - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 6700 XT (AMD Radeon RX 6700 XT; 35.0.99999.9999) - 13th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-13700K (24 threads) - 62.54 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

I'm running Fedora 44.

Proton: experimental-bleeding-edge-11.0-443662-20260930
vkd3d-proton: vkd3d-1.1-5641-g44cf7c204, commit 44cf7c2042168f3b8ee37249f0a53ac091e48fd9

Can confirm that this seems to be fixed with Proton Experimental, suggesting this to be an upstream Proton or Proton dependency bug. Can still repro on Proton 11.0-2. I recommend keeping the bug open to track the upstream issue until the fixes it a mainline Proton release.
